root_cause.text: In gem_get_ethtool_stats(), statistics are copied using the maximum number of queues (MACB_MAX_QUEUES) instead of the actual active queue count (bp->num_queues), causing a buffer size mismatch with gem_get_sset_count() and an out-of-bounds write.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explains: "gem_get_sset_count() correctly computes the number of stats based on the active queues, whereas gem_get_ethtool_stats() indiscriminately copies data using the maximum number of queues." The patch changes `MACB_MAX_QUEUES` to `bp->num_queues` in the memcpy, and the KASAN splat shows a vmalloc-out-of-bounds write in gem_get_ethtool_stats.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the actual number of queues instead of the maximum constant when copying ethtool stats to avoid copying uninitialized or out-of-bounds data.
intent_record.what: Replaced `MACB_MAX_QUEUES` with `bp->num_queues` in the size calculation for `memcpy` in `gem_get_ethtool_stats`.
intent_record.how: The memcpy now copies only the number of bytes corresponding to the actual number of queues on the device, preventing copy of uninitialized or out-of-bounds data when the device has fewer queues than the maximum.
